MC EXCLUSIVE Walmart probes Flipkart employees over kickbacks exceeding Rs 150 crore
The ongoing investigation covers employees in Flipkart’s smartphones, luggage and travel accessories (LTA) divisions and marks the third internal probe Walmart has initiated at the e-commerce company in less than three years over alleged financial misconduct, sources told Moneycontrol.
Tushar Goenka
&
Chandra R Srikanth
October 31, 2026 / 10:54 IST
Such matters are of significance for giants like Walmart, which is listed on the stock exchanges in the US and strictly governed by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
US retail giant Walmart has launched an investigation into alleged wrongdoing at Flipkart following whistleblower complaints that employees in the e-commerce company's smartphones and luggage and travel accessories (LTA) divisions received kickbacks totalling over Rs 150 crore ($16 million), four people aware of the developments told Moneycontrol.
Walmart, which owns more than 80 percent of Flipkart, is the Indian e-commerce major's parent company.
“Investigations are still underway, and the quantum and exact nature of the wrongdoing, including the amount taken by certain employees in kickbacks, will become clear over the coming weeks. Walmart will then take necessary action,” one of the persons cited above said. Two other sources confirmed the details.
“Flipkart has robust governance processes and controls and is committed to the highest standards of integrity and compliance. We take any concerns seriously and address them through established processes. We remain committed to ensuring the highest standards of ethical conduct across our business,” a Flipkart spokesperson said, hours after the story was published.
The arrangement

Kickbacks of this nature are uncommon, particularly at large and reputed companies such as Flipkart, India’s leading e-commerce marketplace ahead of Amazon and Meesho in terms of gross merchandise value (GMV). While the alleged financial misappropriation of around Rs 150 crore (~$16 million) may appear relatively small given Flipkart’s scale - the company reported revenues of over Rs 1.46 lakh crore (over $15 billion) for financial year (FY) 2026 - the incident raises questions about the robustness of its internal controls and processes.
At Flipkart, certain employees were understood to have accepted favours from brands across the smartphones and luggage and travel accessories (LTA) categories in exchange for preferential treatment, sources said.
“The employees were found to be largely exploiting the business-to-business (B2B) route at Flipkart. Some Flipkart employees took a cut from vendors of certain mobile phone brands when devices were moving from one business to another,” a source told Moneycontrol.
“In exchange, these Flipkart employees ensured that sellers received preferential treatment, including greater visibility, on the platform, which resulted in higher sales for the vendors concerned,” another person familiar with the developments said.
Flipkart operates its B2B (business-to-business) operations through two primary channels: Flipkart Wholesale (targeting kiranas, retailers, and MSMEs) and its Flipkart B2B Sales Program for marketplace sellers. This is over and above Flipkart's consumer marketplace arm.
Third such investigation
The probe marks the third investigation Walmart has conducted within Flipkart in less than three years, one of the persons cited above said.
Around two-and-a-half years ago, Walmart had investigated employees in the luggage and travel accessories (LTA) department over financial misappropriation. “Following the investigation, at least three employees were terminated,” a source said.
Then six months ago, Walmart investigated another case of financial wrongdoing in the smartphones division, according to a source. “One employee was found guilty of the charges and chose to resign before they could be fired,” a second source told Moneycontrol.
The details of the first two investigations have not been reported previously.
Such incidents are particularly significant for companies such as Walmart, which is listed in the US and subject to strict norms under the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
Flipkart's winter of discontent
These developments also come at a critical time for Flipkart, which is reeling under a series of senior-level exits, discontent among current and former employees over the liquidity of ESOPs (employee stock ownership plan), and uncertainty surrounding its IPO timeline.
As Moneycontrol exclusively first reported a few months ago, Walmart has yet to decide on a timeline for taking Flipkart public. A growing number of current and former employees are unhappy with the company’s direction, particularly as the delay in an IPO has impacted their expectations around ESOP liquidity.
Consequently, at least 14 vice presidents (VPs) and senior vice presidents (SVPs) have left Flipkart over the past year, sources had earlier told Moneycontrol. At least 1,000 former Flipkart employees had also written to the Walmart board a few weeks ago, seeking parity with current employees in the event of a stock buyback.
